look_here_first: An often tall/sprawling subshrub with opposite toothed 3-veined leaves and multiple fluffy lavender/whitish heads; flip one INDIVIDUAL head sideways: the cylindrical involucre is usually 8–10 mm long, with phyllaries in 4–6(–8) series. Compare shorter, hemispheric Conoclinium heads. Do not identify by flower color or scent alone.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial or subshrub, 80–250 cm, stems erect or spreading/subscandent, short-hairy.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; petioles 5–20 mm; 3-nerved blades, lanceolate to deltate-lanceolate/ovate-lanceolate, 3–10 x 1–4 cm, coarsely toothed to nearly entire.
morphology_keys.heads: Usually 5–50+ small rayless capitula in corymbiform clusters; cylindrical involucres (7–)8–10 mm, phyllaries in 4–6(–8) imbricate series, inner tips appressed/round to truncate.
morphology_keys.corolla: Discoid florets, usually purplish through pale blue, nearly white or pinkish; no ray florets.
morphology_keys.season: Mostly October–December in North American FNA treatment; not exclusionary.
morphology_keys.key_warning: Clusters contain many separate capitula; measure the involucre of ONE capitulum, not the whole cluster.

lookalikes.split: Conoclinium leaves deeply lobed; Chromolaena odorata leaves usually simple toothed. Contrast involucre shape: Conoclinium short/hemispheric, Chromolaena cylindrical 8–10 mm.
Both can have toothed triangular leaves and violet heads; compare one individual involucre and phyllary series, not color; C. coelestinum shorter hemispheric.
Both may be woody-based and have opposite toothed leaves. A. havanensis has much shorter white-head involucres and differs in phyllary/head morphology; stems and bract sides must be photographed.
Herbaceous rhizomatous perennial with broad long-petioled leaves and white heads; inspect stem base and head architecture.

FNA key: almost sessile linear-lanceolate leaves and ± spreading expanded inner phyllary apices; in C. odorata, petioles 5–20 mm, mostly triangular/lanceolate wider leaves, inner phyllary apices appressed.
FNA key: shorter leaf blades 1.5–4 cm and shorter involucres 5.5–7.5(–8) mm; C. odorata usually longer leaves 5–10 cm and involucres 8–10 mm. Occurrence in local region not established.
